title: First Aid at Work
whatItIs: Employers must provide first-aid equipment, facilities and people, so employees injured or taken ill at work get immediate help, and an ambulance in serious cases.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST provide adequate and appropriate first-aid equipment, facilities and suitable people.
Employers MUST tell employees the first-aid arrangements, including where equipment and people are.

keyFacts: The minimum on any site: a stocked first-aid kit, an appointed person and information for workers.
An appointed person takes charge and calls the emergency services. They don't need first-aid training.
First-aid cover is needed whenever people are at work, including shifts, nights and weekends.
Don't keep tablets or medicines in the first-aid box.

visual.caption: Suggested first-aid cover for higher-hazard work such as construction

rows: At least one first-aider trained in EFAW or FAW, depending on the likely injuries
At least one FAW-trained first-aider for every 50 employed (or part of 50)
notes: These numbers are suggestions only: base cover on your first-aid needs assessment.
EFAW = emergency first aid at work. FAW = first aid at work (EFAW plus specific injuries and illness).

a.label: Appointed person
points: Takes charge and calls an ambulance
No first-aid training needed; gives no first aid untrained

b.label: First-aider
points: Trained in FAW, EFAW or another suitable level
Gives first aid and can act as appointed person

onTheTest.question: A construction contractor has 30 workers on site. What first-aid cover does HSE suggest as a minimum?
options: A nurse on site at all times
onTheTest.why: INDG214 Table 2: for higher-hazard work such as construction, with 5 to 50 employees, have at least one first-aider trained in EFAW or FAW.

onTheTest.question: What is the role of an appointed person?
options: Take charge of first aid and call an ambulance
Hand out medicines from the kit
onTheTest.why: An appointed person takes charge of first-aid arrangements, looks after the equipment and calls the emergency services. They shouldn't give first aid they aren't trained for.

traps: An appointed person is not a first-aider and shouldn't give first aid they aren't trained for.
There's no compulsory list of first-aid box contents: it depends on the needs assessment.
Plan cover for first-aiders' annual leave: an appointed person only covers unforeseen absences.
The First-Aid Regulations don't cover the public, but HSE strongly recommends including them in your provision.
